extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of SINGULAR/PLURAL computer-algebra system working with non-commutative Groebner bases and related algorithms (mathematicians, computer-algebra researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/manual chapter describing non-commutative extension libraries (Letterplace, bimodules, bfun, central) for SINGULAR/PLURAL, listing procedures, usage, assumptions, returns, examples and implementation notes for computing two-sided Groebner bases, b-functions, centralizers, and auxiliary routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterplace: compute two-sided Groebner bases up to degree bound
rubrics_metrics.description: With the Letterplace functionality it is possible to compute two-sided Groebner basis of a graded two-sided ideal in a free associative algebra up to a given degree (assumes each variable has degree 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions: stable implementation only for homogeneous input (quasi-homogeneous and general inhomogeneous computations under development; no automatic checks). Because free algebra is not Noetherian, an explicit degree bound must be defined; makeLetterplaceRing stores that bound in the ring structure so letplaceGBasis in such a ring need not be given the bound. Required options: option(redSB); option(redTail); must always be activated. Recommended to run with option(prot); option(mem) to see activity journal and memory usage. Conversion routines available in freegb_lib; freeGBasis can be used to avoid conversion tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: letplaceGBasis / freegb system equivalence and conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure letplaceGBasis computes Groebner bases in the letterplace encoding; alternatively system('freegb',I,d,n) does the same (n = number of variables of original commutative ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is in letterplace encoding. To convert letterplace presentation to strings use lp2lstr and lst2str from freegb lib. Alternatively use freeGBasis (Section 7.7.9) to use a different encoding for polynomials in free algebra so no conversion needed. Example in text shows defining a letterplace ring with makeLetterplaceRing(d), running letplaceGBasis(I), then lp2lstr(J,r); setring r; lst2str(@LN,1) to show string presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: bistd (two-sided Groebner basis via bimodules/enveloping algebra)
rubrics_metrics.description: bistd(M) computes the two-sided Groebner basis of an ideal/module M by using the enveloping algebra of the base ring, as an alternative to twostd().
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: bistd(M); Return: ideal or module (same type as argument). Purpose: compute two-sided Groebner basis of an ideal/module using enveloping algebra approach. Example provided showing load of bimodules.lib, creation of nc algebra and module, and computing M2 = bistd(L). See references for algorithmic origin. Related libraries: ncalg.lib, nctools.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitrinity (coefficient matrix + bisyzygies for two-sided Groebner bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: bitrinity(M) returns the enveloping algebra of the base ring and exports a list L = Coeff, BiSyz where Coeff is a coefficient matrix (first row corresponds to images of Groebner basis) and BiSyz is a bisyzygy matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: bitrinity(M); Return: ring (enveloping algebra) and list L = Coeff, BiSyz. Purpose: provides coefficients that produce the two-sided Groebner basis from original generators and computes bisyzygies of M as left-module over the enveloping algebra. Example shows how to setring G and inspect L[1] (Coeff) and L[2] (BiSyz) and how psi_s maps rows to actual Groebner basis elements. Note: to extract L do def G = bitrinity(); setring G; L;.

rubrics_metrics.name: liftenvelope (compute left-syzygy Groebner basis and coefficient vector for representing g)
rubrics_metrics.description: liftenvelope(M,g) given a two-sided ideal/module M and polynomial g returns the enveloping algebra of the base ring and exports a list l = C, B where B is left Groebner basis of left-syzygies of M ⊗ 1 and C is a vector of coefficients in the enveloping algebra such that psi_s(C^T * (f1 ... fn)) = g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: liftenvelope(M,g); Return: ring (enveloping algebra) and list l = C, B. Purpose: used for computing total divisors; l defines an affine set A = C + sum ai bi such that psi_s(a^T*(f1...fn)) = g for all a in A. If pure tensors are found in A, liftenvelope helps to decide whether f is a total divisor of g. Note: second component has to be an element of first component. Example shows extracting l via setring J; print(l[1]); print(l[2]);.

rubrics_metrics.name: CompDecomp (decompose polynomial in enveloping algebra by right-side tensor factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: CompDecomp(p) (only works when base ring is enveloping algebra A^{env}) returns an ideal I in A^{env} where sum of terms with same right side are grouped as generators, enabling check whether p is a pure tensor and decomposition by right-side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: CompDecomp(p); Return: ideal I. Purpose: decompose polynomial into summands grouped by right-side tensor factors. Example: shows how f decomposes to (x2+5x+1)*SX + x2*S and how CompDecomp yields corresponding ideal generators. Warning: argument polynomial must be in A^{env}.

rubrics_metrics.name: isPureTensor (test and produce decomposition if pure tensor)
rubrics_metrics.description: isPureTensor(g) returns 0 if g is not a pure tensor; if g is a pure tensor it returns a vector v with v = a*gen(1) + b*gen(2) = (a,b)^T with a (X) b = g (works only if basering is enveloping algebra).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isPureTensor(g). Return: 0 or vector v representing decomposition. Purpose: check whether polynomial in A^{env} is a pure tensor; auxiliary for total divisibility testing. Examples show outputs for various polynomials, illustrating when 0 is returned and when a decomposition vector is returned. Note: basering must be A^{env}.

rubrics_metrics.name: isTwoSidedGB (check whether ideal generators are two-sided)
rubrics_metrics.description: isTwoSidedGB(I) returns 1 if the generators of given ideal I are two-sided, 0 otherwise. Intended for non-commutative rings (in commutative rings every element is two-sided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isTwoSidedGB(I); Return: int 0/1. Purpose: auxiliary procedure for diagonal forms to check Rp = pR. Examples: shows cases returning 1 and 0. Note: should only be used for non-commutative rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: bfct (compute roots and multiplicities of Bernstein-Sato polynomial b(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: bfct(f [,s,t,v]) computes the roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial b(s) for hypersurface defined by f; returns list containing ideal of roots and intvec of multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: bfct(f[,s,t,v]); Return: list of ideal (roots) and intvec (multiplicities). Assume: basering commutative of characteristic 0. Background: computes initial Malgrange ideal per Noro's algorithm and solves linear system by linear reductions. Options: if s<>0 std used for GB, else slimgb; if t<>0 matrix ordering used for GB else block ordering; v positive weight vector used for homogenization. Display controlled by printlevel. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: bfctSyz (compute b(s) roots via syzygies)
rubrics_metrics.description: bfctSyz(f [,r,s,t,u,v]) computes roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomial using syzygy computations (initial Malgrange ideal then solve linear system by computing syzygies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: bfctSyz(f[,r,s,t,u,v]); Return: list of ideal (roots) and intvec (multiplicities). Assume: basering commutative, char 0. Options: r,t,u control using std vs slimgb in char 0 or >0; s controls matrix vs block ordering; v positive weight vector for homogenization. Display controlled by printlevel. Examples given.

rubrics_metrics.name: bfctAnn (compute b(s) roots via Ann(f^s) computation)
rubrics_metrics.description: bfctAnn(f [,a,b,c]) computes roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomial by computing Ann(f^s) and solving linear equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: bfctAnn(f[,a,b,c]); Return: list ideal and intvec. Assume: basering commutative, char 0. Notes: if a<>0 only f appended to Ann(f^s), else f and all partial derivatives appended. b and c control choice of GB engine (std vs slimgb) and behavior for computing ideals <I+J>. Display controlled by printlevel. Examples provided (including Reiffen curve).

rubrics_metrics.name: bfctOneGB (compute b(s) roots using single Groebner basis computation)
rubrics_metrics.description: bfctOneGB(f [,s,t]) computes roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomial using only one Groebner-basis computation by combining Noro's method with an elimination ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: bfctOneGB(f[,s,t]); Return: list ideal and intvec. Assume: basering commutative, char 0. Notes: s,t control GB engine and ordering (std/slimgb, matrix/block). Display controlled by printlevel. Example shows typical outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: bfctIdeal (global b-function of a holonomic ideal w.r.t. weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: bfctIdeal(I,w[,s,t]) computes roots of global b-function of holonomic ideal I in Weyl algebra with respect to weight (-w,w). Returns L[1] ideal of rational roots, L[2] intvec of multiplicities, optional L[3] part without rational roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: bfctIdeal(I,w[,s,t]); Return: list L as described. Assume: basering is n-th Weyl algebra in char 0, variables ordered x(1..n),D(1..n) with standard commutation, I holonomic. Notes: If b-function degree 0 encoded specially (L[1][1]=0,L[2]=0,L[3]=1 or 0). s,t control GB engines and orderings. If input ideal not holonomic, warnings appear and degree bound may be set. Display controlled by printlevel. Examples show behavior on holonomic and non-holonomic examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: pIntersect (intersection of ideal with subalgebra K[f])
rubrics_metrics.description: pIntersect(f,I[,s]) computes the intersection of ideal I with subalgebra K[f] and returns coefficient vector of monic polynomial generator (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: pIntersect(f,I[,s]); Return: vector (coefficient vector of monic polynomial). Assume: I given as Groebner basis, basering not a qring. Note: if intersection is zero, proc might not terminate. If s>0 searches only up to degree s; otherwise no bound. Display controlled by printlevel. Example shows pIntersect(t*Dt,inF) returning gen(4)-1/36*gen(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: pIntersectSyz (intersection via syzygies and optional modular step)
rubrics_metrics.description: pIntersectSyz(f,I[,p,s,t]) computes intersection of ideal I with K[f] using syzygies; if p (prime) provided computes generator mod p first and then lifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: pIntersectSyz(f,I[,p,s,t]); Return: vector (coefficient vector). Assume: I given as Groebner basis. Notes: If p>0 computes in char p first then searches in basering for that degree; otherwise computes syzygies searching all degrees. s,t control choice of GB engine (std/slimgb) in different char settings. Display controlled by printlevel. Examples provided showing working with a specific prime and returning same generator.

rubrics_metrics.name: linReduce (linear reduction of polynomial by ideal elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: linReduce(f,I[,s,t,u]) reduces polynomial f only by linear reductions (no monomial multiplications); can return reduced polynomial and coefficient vector of used reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: linReduce(f,I[,s,t,u]); Return: poly or list (reduced polynomial and optional coeﬃcient vector). Notes: s<>0 returns list with reduced poly and coeﬃcient vector; t<>0 (default) reduces all monomials if possible, else only leading monomials; u<>0 (default) uses linearly pre-reduced ideal via linReduceIdeal; if u=0 and ideal differs from linReduceIdeal result, outcome may be unexpected. Display controlled by printlevel. Examples show various reduction modes and verification that f - (l[1] - (M*l[2])[1,1]) = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: linReduceIdeal (linear pre-reduction of an ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: linReduceIdeal(I[,s,t,u]) performs linear reductions on list of polynomials in I (no monomial multiplications) and returns reduced ideal or list including coefficient vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: linReduceIdeal(I[,s,t,u]); Return: ideal or list (reduced ideal and optionally coefficient module). Notes: s<>0 returns list with reduced ideal and coefficient vectors; t<>0 default reduces tails also; u<>0 default sorts ideal in increasing order before reduction (if u=0 and ideal not sorted as expected, result may differ). Display controlled by printlevel. Examples illustrate tail reductions and verification of module relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: linSyzSolve (compute linear syzygy among ideal elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: linSyzSolve(I[,s]) computes a linear dependency between elements of ideal I if one exists and returns the coefficient vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: linSyzSolve(I[,s]); Return: vector (coefficient vector of linear combination equalling 0). Notes: s<>0 toggles std vs slimgb for Groebner computations (default slimgb in char 0, std in char >0). Examples show gen(2)-2*gen(1) for I = (x,2x) and 0 for independent generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: allPositive (check positivity of intvec components)
rubrics_metrics.description: allPositive(v) returns 1 if all components of intvec v are positive, otherwise 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: allPositive(v); Return: int 0/1. Purpose: simple helper to check positivity. Examples: v = 1,2,3 returns 1; w = 1,-2,3 returns 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: scalarProd (scalar product of two intvecs)
rubrics_metrics.description: scalarProd(v,w) returns standard scalar product of intvecs v and w; assumes same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: scalarProd(v,w); Return: int (scalar product). Assume: arguments same size. Example: scalarProd(1,2,3 ; 4,5,6) returns 32.

rubrics_metrics.name: vec2poly (construct univariate polynomial from vector coefficients)
rubrics_metrics.description: vec2poly(v[,i]) constructs an univariate polynomial in variable var(i) whose coefficients are given by vector v; default i=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: vec2poly(v[,i]); Return: poly in K[var(i)]. Purpose: construct polynomial such that coefficient at var(i)^{j-1} is v[j]. Examples: vec2poly(intvec 3,2,1) -> x^2+2x+3; vec2poly with vector of ring elements constructs polynomial with those coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: centralizeSet (compute centralizer basis in vector space spanned by V)
rubrics_metrics.description: centralizeSet(F,V) computes a vector space basis of the centralizer of set F in the vector space generated by V over the ground field; returns ideal generated by computed elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: centralizeSet(F,V); Return: ideal of computed centralizing elements. Purpose: find centralizer basis within span(V). Example demonstrates computing PBW_maxMonom to generate V, calling centralizeSet and verifying with inCenter(C). See related procedures centralizer, centralizerVS, inCentralizer.

rubrics_metrics.name: centralizerVS (compute centralizer up to degree D)
rubrics_metrics.description: centralizerVS(F,D) computes vector space basis of centralizer(F) up to degree D (D non-negative) and returns ideal of generators found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: centralizerVS(F,D); Return: ideal of computed elements. Purpose: compute centralizer truncated by degree bound. Note: D must be non-negative. Example finds elements commuting with x and y up to degree 4 and verifies with inCentralizer.

rubrics_metrics.name: centralizerRed (compute subalgebra generators of centralizer up to termination criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: centralizerRed(F,D[,N]) computes subalgebra generators of centralizer(F) up to degree D or stops when at least N elements are found (if D positive or D negative combined with N determines termination). Current ordering must be degree-compatible well-ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: centralizerRed(F,D[,N]); Return: ideal of computed subalgebra generators. Purpose: compute subalgebra generators of centralizer(F) with termination conditions since centralizer(F) may be infinite. Notes/warnings: If D positive only elements up to degree D computed; if D negative termination determined by N. If N larger than actual number of generators, procedure may not terminate. Example provided computing generators for U(sl_2).
